picks.file: Civitates orbis terrarum. Urbium praecipuarum totius mundi. Liber quartus (page 104).jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye plan, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 4
picks.why: colored copy (1594 printing) of the 1588 plate; walled town with buildings drawn, Roman amphitheater oval recognizable; book margins trimmed

picks.file: Vista di Lucca dal campanile di Santi Giovanni e Reparata 02.jpg
picks.what: The cathedral of San Martino, photograph from the bell tower of Santi Giovanni e Reparata
picks.why: sharp color view of the cathedral and its square, the city’s main landmark

gaps: P0: none. P2: none. P3: only the 1845 Nottolini aqueduct print (#7), which shows the countryside, not the city. P4: none. P5: none.
notes: The B&H plate is a perspective plan with buildings drawn in elevation rather than a true bird’s-eye view; #4 (BnF loose plate) has a strong center fold and #2 is an uncolored open book, so #1 is the best copy. #3 is Linz, #5 and #6 are Luca Bertelli prints of saints, #8 is a Goya portrait. P6 alternative: #10 (rooftop view toward San Frediano and the Torre delle Ore) is a more general view but the landmarks are small; #11 and #12 are hazy.
